question: What is the minimum attendance requirement at VIT Chennai?
answer: You need at least 75% attendance in every course (up to 25% absence, which covers medical, personal, casual and official leave such as event organising or co-curricular participation). Attendance is checked separately for CAT-I, CAT-II and FAT, counted from the date you registered for the course up to one day before the exam component (for FAT, up to the last instructional day). If you fall below 75% you are debarred from the next exam component; debarred from FAT means an N grade and you must re-register. Students with CGPA 9.00 or above and no current backlog are exempt from the minimum attendance rule (not in the summer semester), and the exemption is rechecked before each CAT/FAT.
source: VIT Chennai FFCS Academic Regulations v5.0, Section 8 and Table 2 (Academic Council, 20.11.2025) - https://chennai.vit.ac.in/files/Academic-Regulations-5.0.pdf

question: How do I check my class timetable?

First-semester courses are registered for you by the School Academic Coordinator; from the second semester you choose your own slots. View your personal timetable after logging in to the official student login (VTOP) at https://vtopcc.vit.ac.in/. Confirm any room or time change with your faculty or school.

question: What should I know about the exam format (CAT and FAT) before an exam?
answer: For theory courses: each CAT is 90 minutes for 50 marks (scaled to 15), CAT-II is open book/open notebook (any books and handwritten notebooks), and the FAT is 3 hours for 100 marks. Continuous assessment makes up 60% and the FAT 40% of the total. You can be debarred from an exam for attendance shortage, indiscipline or course withdrawal. Scribe or extra time (maximum 30 minutes for a 3-hour FAT) is given only for specified medical conditions with a medical certificate submitted through your Proctor and HoD to the School Dean. Follow the specific instructions issued for each exam.

question: How do I apply for a re-evaluation?
answer: After FAT marks are published you can apply to see your FAT answer script and, if you find a discrepancy, apply for re-evaluation within the period announced by the Institute and by paying the prescribed fee. If re-evaluation changes your marks by up to 5% the better of the two is taken; if the change is more than 5% a different examiner evaluates it and the best of three is taken. If you are still dissatisfied you may apply to the Examination Appellate Committee (two faculty members) with the necessary fee; its decision is final. There is no re-evaluation for lab/practical exams, soft skills, project viva, seminar/design or project-type components. Grades are reassigned on the original grade bands.
source: VIT Chennai FFCS Academic Regulations v5.0, Section 9.9 (Academic Council, 20.11.2025) - https://chennai.vit.ac.in/files/Academic-Regulations-5.0.pdf

question: How do I apply for leave and what counts as absence?
answer: There is no separate leave quota: up to 25% absence per course (medical, personal, casual or official leave) is already built into the 75% attendance rule. If you attend on an institute sectional holiday declared as an instructional day, send a request to your HoD through your Proctor to consider your attendance. If you miss the FAT after hospitalization of more than a week or a death in the family, apply for Re-FAT within 14 calendar days with a certificate authenticated by the Chief Medical Officer.

You must finish all required courses and credits, and the maximum period is the minimum duration plus 3 years, after which studentship is cancelled.
source: VIT Chennai FFCS Academic Regulations v5.0, Sections 4.1, 19 and Annexure 1 (Academic Council, 20.11.2025) - https://chennai.vit.ac.in/files/Academic-Regulations-5.0.pdf

question: How many credits can I register per semester?
answer: The average academic load is 23 credits per regular semester; you can register a minimum of 16 and a maximum of 27 credits (the last registration of the programme may be below 16). There is no minimum or maximum in the summer semester if courses are offered and timetables do not clash. One credit means one 50-minute lecture or tutorial per week, or 100 minutes of lab per week, over a 15-week semester.
source: VIT Chennai FFCS Academic Regulations v5.0, Sections 6.1 and 7.3 (Academic Council, 20.11.2025) - https://chennai.vit.ac.in/files/Academic-Regulations-5.0.pdf

question: What happens if I am debarred or get an N grade?
answer: An N grade carries zero grade points. N1 means one or more components (theory or lab) not cleared, N2 means debarred from FAT for attendance shortage, N3 means absent in FAT, and N4 means debarred for indiscipline or exam malpractice. To clear it you must re-register in a later semester and earn a performance grade; N1 components you already cleared are exempted from re-registration. Students with F, N1 or N3 can alternatively use the arrear examination after the final semester.
source: VIT Chennai FFCS Academic Regulations v5.0, Sections 7.4 and 9.4 (Academic Council, 20.11.2025) - https://chennai.vit.ac.in/files/Academic-Regulations-5.0.pdf

question: How are grades awarded at VIT?
keywords: grading|grade points|S grade|relative grading|absolute grading|letter grade
answer: Performance grades are S (10), A (9), B (8), C (7), D (6) and E (5); F gives zero. Theory classes with more than 10 students use relative grading based on the class mean and standard deviation, with S needing at least 90% marks. Classes of 10 or fewer, labs, soft skills and project courses use absolute grading: S at 90 or above, A 80-89, B 70-79, C 60-69, D 55-59, E 50-54 and F below 50.
source: VIT Chennai FFCS Academic Regulations v5.0, Sections 9.4 to 9.6 (Tables 4 to 6) (Academic Council, 20.11.2025) - https://chennai.vit.ac.in/files/Academic-Regulations-5.0.pdf

question: What are the passing criteria?
answer: You must score at least 40% in the theory FAT alone, and at least 50% of the marks in lab and/or project components. For courses other than theory-only, you also need at least 50% of the grand total. For theory-only courses the pass mark follows the relative grading band. There are no minimum marks for continuous assessment (CAM). Failing gives an F grade.
source: VIT Chennai FFCS Academic Regulations v5.0, Section 9.4 (Academic Council, 20.11.2025) - https://chennai.vit.ac.in/files/Academic-Regulations-5.0.pdf

question: How is CGPA calculated and converted to a percentage?
answer: GPA is the credit-weighted average of grade points for a semester, and CGPA is the credit-weighted average across all courses since the first semester (courses repeated after an F count only once). Pass-fail, audit, minor, honours and second major courses are excluded. Percentage equivalent is CGPA x 10 (for example 8.75 CGPA = 87.5%), and the Controller of Examinations issues a certificate on request.
source: VIT Chennai FFCS Academic Regulations v5.0, Section 9.10 (Academic Council, 20.11.2025) - https://chennai.vit.ac.in/files/Academic-Regulations-5.0.pdf

question: What is the make-up examination?
answer: If you get an F or N1 grade in a theory-only or theory-with-embedded-lab course, you can apply for the Make-up Examination conducted by the Controller of Examinations, in any number of such courses from your recently published results. The maximum grade you can get is E. If you fail it, you must re-register for the course in a later semester. F, N1 and N3 courses can also be cleared through the arrear examination after the final semester.
source: VIT Chennai FFCS Academic Regulations v5.0, Sections 7.4 and 9.12 (Academic Council, 20.11.2025) - https://chennai.vit.ac.in/files/Academic-Regulations-5.0.pdf

question: What if I miss a CAT or the FAT?
answer: If you miss a CAT, its weightage is forfeited and generally no re-CAT is held; a Re-CAT is available for CAT-I in unavoidable circumstances, for hospitalization or health reasons, and for missing it due to internships or placement activity (provided attendance requirement is met). For the FAT, a Re-FAT is possible only after hospitalization of more than a week or a death in the family, applied for within 14 calendar days with proper evidence; if you do not appear for the scheduled Re-FAT, your N grade stays.
source: VIT Chennai FFCS Academic Regulations v5.0, Sections 9.4 and 9.11 (Academic Council, 20.11.2025) - https://chennai.vit.ac.in/files/Academic-Regulations-5.0.pdf

question: What if my internal assessment marks look wrong?
answer: Internal assessment marks appear in your student login at least one week before the FAT. Report any discrepancy to the course faculty immediately; if unresolved, escalate to your Proctor, HoD or School Dean within two days from the start of the FAT. Later requests are not considered.
source: VIT Chennai FFCS Academic Regulations v5.0, Section 9.8 (Academic Council, 20.11.2025) - https://chennai.vit.ac.in/files/Academic-Regulations-5.0.pdf

question: What is the penalty for academic malpractice?
answer: Cases go to a Malpractice Committee. Malpractice in a CAT or other continuous assessment component gives zero marks in that exam for all subjects registered that semester. Malpractice in the FAT gives an N grade in all regular courses you were eligible to write that semester; you can clear them later by re-registering. Submitting a purchased, borrowed or previously submitted project is malpractice and results in an N grade.
source: VIT Chennai FFCS Academic Regulations v5.0, Sections 6.3.1.2 and 9.14 (Academic Council, 20.11.2025) - https://chennai.vit.ac.in/files/Academic-Regulations-5.0.pdf

question: What are F and N backlogs and how do I clear them?
answer: An F grade is a backlog; N grades are incomplete courses; W-grade courses are not backlogs. You can register for the next-level course even with an F in the prerequisite. Clear F or N1 through the one-time make-up exam, or by re-registering (a re-registration fee applies); F, N1 and N3 can also be cleared via the arrear exam after the final semester, where all components must be registered. Backlog courses cannot be withdrawn.
source: VIT Chennai FFCS Academic Regulations v5.0, Sections 7.4, 7.6 and 7.7 (Academic Council, 20.11.2025) - https://chennai.vit.ac.in/files/Academic-Regulations-5.0.pdf

question: How does grade improvement work?
answer: You may register again for the same course at a later registration to improve your grade, paying the course fee; it is treated as a separate course within the credit limits. It can be used only once per course and for one course per semester, although graduating-year and timed-out students may take more than one.
source: VIT Chennai FFCS Academic Regulations v5.0, Section 15 (Academic Council, 20.11.2025) - https://chennai.vit.ac.in/files/Academic-Regulations-5.0.pdf

question: Can I withdraw from a course?
answer: Yes. After CAT-I marks are finalised, withdrawal is open for three instructional days. Withdrawal below 16 credits is generally not allowed (final-year and timed-out students are exempt). A withdrawn course shows a W grade, is not counted in GPA and cannot be reinstated; backlog courses cannot be withdrawn and no refund is made for additional or re-registered courses.
source: VIT Chennai FFCS Academic Regulations v5.0, Section 7.6 (Academic Council, 20.11.2025) - https://chennai.vit.ac.in/files/Academic-Regulations-5.0.pdf

question: How do audit courses work?
answer: You need a CGPA of 8.0 or more at registration. B.Tech and 5-year integrated students can audit at most two courses in the whole programme, one per semester (more in the graduating year). Audit courses must be marked at registration, follow the same 75% attendance and assessment rules, appear as a U grade if completed, and do not count in CGPA. UC/PC/PE courses in your own curriculum cannot be audited.
source: VIT Chennai FFCS Academic Regulations v5.0, Section 10 (Academic Council, 20.11.2025) - https://chennai.vit.ac.in/files/Academic-Regulations-5.0.pdf

question: What are Minor, Honours and Second Major credentials?
answer: These are extra credentials earned by registering additional courses from the 3rd semester onwards, without exceeding the 27-credit cap. A Minor is in another discipline (about 18-20 credits; you need a minimum 7.50 CGPA in minor courses). Honours is in your own discipline (minimum 18 credits). A Second Major needs 40 credits of Programme Core courses of another programme. Their grades do not affect your CGPA. Ancillary and Additional Concentration (20 credits each) from open electives appear only in the transcript.
source: VIT Chennai FFCS Academic Regulations v5.0, Sections 6.3.4 and 13 (Academic Council, 20.11.2025) - https://chennai.vit.ac.in/files/Academic-Regulations-5.0.pdf

question: How does the Semester Abroad Program (SAP) work?
answer: B.Tech students can go abroad in the 6th to 8th semester with CGPA 7 or more and no current F/N backlogs, to partner universities or QS/THE/Shanghai-ranked universities. Duration is one to two semesters, up to 21 credits can be transferred (Professional Elective or Open Elective only), and the grades count toward CGPA. The Office of International Relations handles the application process.
source: VIT Chennai FFCS Academic Regulations v5.0, Section 16.2 (Academic Council, 20.11.2025) - https://chennai.vit.ac.in/files/Academic-Regulations-5.0.pdf

question: Can I take NPTEL (SWAYAM) courses for credit?
answer: Yes, with prior approval from your School Academic Coordinator, one course per semester, and only for Open Elective credits. A 4/8/12/16-week course earns 1/2/3/4 credits. Those credits do not count toward the semester's maximum credit limit, grade improvement is not available, and you must upload the hall ticket, fee receipt and certificate on VTOP. The exam must not clash with your regular exam schedule.
source: VIT Chennai FFCS Academic Regulations v5.0, Sections 6.3.4 and 16.1 (Academic Council, 20.11.2025) - https://chennai.vit.ac.in/files/Academic-Regulations-5.0.pdf

question: What is the Honours Club?
answer: Students with CGPA 9.25 or above, no F grade and never debarred for attendance or indiscipline are admitted. Benefits include preference when the Institute sponsors students to seminars or conferences, a Certificate of Merit, and a cash award or scholarship for later semesters. Admission is withdrawn if you stop meeting the conditions.
source: VIT Chennai FFCS Academic Regulations v5.0, Section 18 (Academic Council, 20.11.2025) - https://chennai.vit.ac.in/files/Academic-Regulations-5.0.pdf

question: Is an internship or project compulsory?
answer: Yes. All students must complete a four-week industrial internship (one block or two 2-week blocks) any time after the first year, keep a digital log, and upload the report and completion certificate to the academic portal; marks come from the log, report and viva. B.Tech students also do an Internship II / Capstone Project, usually registered in the final semester and not allowed during summer semesters.
source: VIT Chennai FFCS Academic Regulations v5.0, Sections 6.3.1.1 and 6.3.1.2 (Academic Council, 20.11.2025) - https://chennai.vit.ac.in/files/Academic-Regulations-5.0.pdf

question: What is the Break of Study rule?
keywords: break of study|medical break|study break|prolonged illness|time limit
answer: If prolonged illness or another valid reason makes you miss more than 25% of classes, you may request a Break of Study (maximum one year, once in the programme) recommended by your School Dean and approved by the Dean Academics, and the time limit for completing the programme extends by the break period. Being debarred for attendance or indiscipline does not count as a break. If you drop a semester after it starts, fees are not refunded.
source: VIT Chennai FFCS Academic Regulations v5.0, Section 19 (Academic Council, 20.11.2025) - https://chennai.vit.ac.in/files/Academic-Regulations-5.0.pdf
